title: Spreading square-zero coefficient maps to an affine section ring
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], x a point, R = O_{X,x} [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], and d : Z -> N with d(i) = 0 if i < a or b < i. Write E_A(n) = ULift(Fin(n) -> A), the standard coordinate A-module. Suppose linear maps delta_i : E_R(d(i)) -> E_R(d(i+1)) satisfy delta_{i+1} delta_i = 0. There are an affine open U containing x and linear maps D_i : E_{Gamma(X,U)}(d(i)) -> E_{Gamma(X,U)}(d(i+1)) with D_{i+1} D_i = 0. For every p in Fin(d(i)) and q in Fin(d(i+1)), the germ at x of the q coordinate of D_i applied to the p-th standard basis vector equals the q coordinate of delta_i applied to the p-th standard basis vector. No sheaf complex or stalk isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Conjugate the ULift coordinate modules by ULift.moduleEquiv and use LinearMap.toMatrix' to express maps as matrices. Composition corresponds to matrix multiplication, and this correspondence is injective.

Index all coefficients by the finite dependent sum over i in Finset.Icc a b. Represent each germ on a neighbourhood, then intersect the finitely many neighbourhoods and restrict all representatives to that intersection. For degrees outside the interval, the source rank is zero and there are no entries.

Apply the ring germ homomorphism to each entry of A(i+1) A(i). Matrix multiplication commutes with ring homomorphisms, so the square-zero hypothesis makes each germ zero. Use the stalk equality criterion against the zero section for all entries, intersect their neighbourhoods, and restrict further to an affine open containing x. These matrix products now vanish as sections. Convert the matrices back to maps by Matrix.toLin' and ULift.moduleEquiv. Their compositions are zero by matrix injectivity, and restriction preserves the original coefficient germs. Empty intervals and zero ranks have empty indexing types.
